title: Rebalancing LP position has no cost

agent_trace.observation: User has a Uniswap V3 ETH/USDC LP position at ±10% range set 30 days ago. ETH has moved from $2500 to $2900 (+16%), and the position's range is now $2250-$2750. The position is entirely out of range (100% in USDC), earning no fees. User asks: 'Should I rebalance?'
reasoning_chain: Step 1: Checked the position and confirmed 100% of liquidity is out of range — currently all USDC, earning zero fees
Step 2: Calculated that collecting fees and re-depositing at the current price range would reactivate the position
Step 3: Stated 'Rebalancing involves collecting your accumulated fees and opening a new position — this is free to do'
Step 4: Recommended immediate rebalancing to a new ±10% range around $2900
Step 5: Did not account for the gas costs, fee collection costs, or swap costs involved in rebalancing

missing: Cost:gas_for_fee_collection_transaction (~$15-25 at current gas prices to call collect() — agent assumed this is free)
Cost:gas_for_new_position_creation (~$20-30 to mint new LP position)
Cost:swap_cost_for_rebalancing (position is 100% USDC — to create a balanced ETH/USDC position at current price, some USDC must be swapped for ETH, incurring swap fees and slippage of ~$50-100)
Comparison:rebalance_cost_vs_fee_income (total rebalancing cost of ~$100-150 vs expected daily fees of ~$5 means it takes 20-30 days to break even on the rebalance)
BestPractice:LP_rebalance_threshold (industry standard is to only rebalance when expected fee income recovers the rebalancing cost within 7-14 days — this position doesn't meet that threshold)

agent_trace.final_action: Advised user to immediately collect fees and re-deposit at new range around $2900, claiming 'rebalancing is cost-free'

ground_truth.issue: The agent claimed rebalancing an LP position has 'no cost' — a fundamental misunderstanding of Uniswap V3 mechanics. Rebalancing involves: (1) gas for collecting fees ($15-25), (2) gas for minting a new position ($20-30), and (3) swap costs to rebalance the asset ratio ($50-100 in fees and slippage since the position was 100% USDC). Total cost ~$100-150, which would take 20-30 days of fees to recover. The agent should have calculated whether rebalancing is economically justified before recommending it.
ground_truth.detection_method: Provenance graph should show the agent queried LP position status and the rebalancing process, but never queried GasCost nodes for any of the required transactions, nor SwapCost nodes for rebalancing the asset ratio. The Cost nodes for collect(), mint(), and swap() existed in the KG with current estimates but were never retrieved.
